questions.question: Explain the Schottky defect.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the Schottky defect. / [CO1]
  • A Schottky defect is a type of point defect in an ionic crystal in which an equal number of cations and anions are
  • missing from their normal lattice sites.
  • • Equal numbers of positive and negative ions are absent from the crystal lattice.
  • • Electrical neutrality is maintained because the number of missing cations and anions is equal.
  • • The density of the crystal decreases because some ions are missing from the lattice.
  • • The stoichiometry of the crystal remains unchanged. Examples: NaCl, KCl, KBr and CsCl.
  • (proper explanation can be given full credit, illustration with diagram can also be considered
  • for giving credit)

questions.question: (a) Explain in detail the law of rational indices. (b) Write a short note on Weiss indices and Miller indices.
questions.solution_html:
• (a) Explain in detail the law of rational indices. (b) Write a short note on Weiss indices and Miller
  • indices. / [CO1]
  • (a) Law of Rational Indices: The intercepts made by any crystal face on the crystallographic axes, when expressed
  • in terms of the unit cell parameters, are either infinite or simple rational multiples of those parameters. If a crystal
  • face cuts the three crystallographic axes at the following distances: Along the a-axis: 2a, Along the b-axis: 3b,
  • Along the c-axis: c. The intercepts are therefore:2a:3b:c. (4 marks)
  • (b) Weiss indices: Weiss indices represent a crystal face by expressing its intercepts on the crystallographic axes
  • as multiples of the unit cell dimensions.
  • Method: Determine the intercepts of the crystal face along the a, b and c axes. Express the intercepts in terms of
  • the corresponding unit cell parameters. Write the intercepts as a ratio. Example: If a crystal face cuts the axes at
  • 2a, 3b and c, its Weiss indices are [2:3:1].
  • Miller indices: Miller indices are a set of three smallest integers, represented as (hkl), used to specify the
  • orientation of a crystal plane.
  • Steps for determining Miller indices: Determine the intercepts of the plane along the a, b and c axes in terms of
  • the unit cell parameters. Take the reciprocals of the intercepts. Multiply the reciprocals by a suitable common
  • factor to obtain the smallest whole numbers. Enclose the resulting integers in parentheses as (hkl).
  • Example: Suppose a crystal face has intercepts 2a, 3b and c. The intercepts are: [2,3,1]. Their Miller indices are
  • (326). (6 marks) (Reasonable explanation with suitable example can be given full credits)

questions.question: Derive Gibbs-Helmholtz equation.
questions.solution_html: • Derive Gibbs-Helmholtz equation. / [CO4] Gibbs energy with temp at const pressure: G = H − TS ∵ H = U + PV G = U + PV − TS dG = dU + PdV + VdP − TdS − SdT From 1st law dq = dU + PdV From 2 nd law dqrev = TdS Thus TdS = dU + PdV Subst in eqn for dG, dG = VdP − SdT At const pressure dG = −SdT (dP = 0) ⇒ ቀ ∂ீ ∂Tቁ௉ = −𝑆 For state 1: ቀ ∂ீభ ∂T ቁ௉ = −𝑆¹ state 2: ቀ ∂ீమ ∂T ቁ௉ = −𝑆² ቀ ∂ீమ ∂T ቁ௉ − ቀ ∂ீభ ∂T ቁ௉ = −(𝑆² − 𝑆¹) ቀ ∂(ீమ-ீభ) ∂T ቁ௉ = −∆𝑆 ቀ ∂(∆ீ) ∂T ቁ௉ = −∆𝑆 We know that ΔG=ΔH-TΔS ∆ 𝐺 = ∆𝐻 + 𝑇 ቀ ∂(∆ீ) ∂T ቁ௉ This is known as Gibbs-Helmholtz equation in terms of Gibbs energy and enthalpy change at constant pressure. (Derivation with proper steps can be given full credit)

questions.question: Derive Gibbs-Duhem equation. [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Derive Gibbs-Duhem equation. / [CO4]
  • Gibbs energy (G) is a function of T , P and the number of moles (𝑛¹, 𝑛², … )of the constituents present.
  • 𝐺 = 𝜙(𝑇, 𝑃, 𝑛¹, 𝑛², … )
  • A small change in the Gibbs energy 𝑑𝐺(a complete differential) can be expressed as:
  • 𝑑𝐺 = ൬𝜕𝐺𝜕𝑇൰௉,ⁿభ,ⁿమ,… 𝑑𝑇 + ൬𝜕𝐺𝜕𝑃൰T,ⁿభ,ⁿమ,… 𝑑𝑃 + ൬ 𝜕𝐺𝜕𝑛¹൰T,௉,ⁿమ,ⁿయ,… 𝑑𝑛¹ + ⋯
  • Representing the (𝜕𝐺/𝜕𝑛௜)terms by 𝜇௜, eqn. (b) may be written as:
  • 𝑑𝐺 = ൬𝜕𝐺𝜕𝑇൰௉,ⁿభ,ⁿమ,… 𝑑𝑇 + ൬𝜕𝐺𝜕𝑃൰T,ⁿభ,ⁿమ,… 𝑑𝑃 + 𝜇¹𝑑𝑛¹ + 𝜇²𝑑𝑛² + ⋯
  • For a system at constant T and P (i.e., when 𝑑𝑇 = 0and 𝑑𝑃 = 0), eqn. (c) simpliϐies to:
  • 𝑑𝐺 = 𝜇¹𝑑𝑛¹ + 𝜇²𝑑𝑛² + ⋯
  • For a system of de ϐinite composition, integration of eqn. (d) gives: 𝐺 = 𝜇¹𝑛¹ + 𝜇²𝑛² + ⋯
  • When eqn. (e) is differentiated completely, we get: 𝑑𝐺 = 𝜇¹𝑑𝑛¹ + 𝑛¹𝑑𝜇¹ + 𝜇²𝑑𝑛² + 𝑛²𝑑𝜇²+. .
  • But according to eqn. (c), for a system of deϐinite composition at constant T and P:
  • 𝑑𝐺 = 𝜇¹𝑑𝑛¹ + 𝜇²𝑑𝑛² + ⋯
  • Comparing, we get: 𝑛¹𝑑𝜇¹ + 𝑛²𝑑𝜇² + ⋯ = 0 ∑ 𝑛௜ 𝑑𝜇௜ = 0
  • This equation is called Gibbs–Duhem equation. (Derivation with proper steps can be given full credit)
